keyAssumptions: NMRK Argus: 11-year projection from 1/1/2027; Year 1 NOI $4,195,339 (In-Place NOI as of 1/1/2027 $4,199,349); 10-yr NOI CAGR 2.8%.
Credit loss 0.5% in Year 1, then 3.0% general vacancy, EXCLUDING Advance Auto, Atlantic Union Bank, Floor & Decor, Goodwill, Harbor Freight, Lidl, Mattress Warehouse, Ollie's, Starbucks and Verizon.
Every tenant assumed to exercise its renewal options; no-option tenants renew at market with 75% probability.
Floor & Decor (est. RCD Nov-2026) treated as in place; Seller to credit delivery costs and gap rent at closing.
Verizon Wireless (lease expires Jan-2027) assumed to renew per 'latest renewal discussions with Seller' — not an executed renewal.
Suite 203 (1,975 SF) leases up Jan-2028 at $33.77 PSF with $20 PSF TI.
OpEx per Seller's 2026 budget, +3.0%/yr; management fee 3.0% of EGI; capital reserve $0.15 PSF; no CapEx assumed.

Historical NOI: FY2023 $3,261,860; FY2024 $3,363,364; FY2025 $3,734,776. FY2025 includes $230,740 of 'Other Income' (vs $22,073 in FY2024), which looks non-recurring; the Year 1 pro forma carries none.
Real estate taxes: $355,043 (FY23) → $410,949 (FY24) → $500,040 (FY25) → $625,819 underwritten Year 1 (+25% vs FY25). Two main tax parcels; most tenants reimburse their parcel's pro-rata share.
Unpriced: the OM states no asking price or cap rate.
Suite labels follow the OM tenant roster and site plan (1A Harbor Freight, 1B Goodwill, 1C Ollie's, 1D Lidl, 16A Aspen, 16B Starbucks). The DTU uses different Argus suite IDs (0001A–D, PAD1, PAD1A).
Tenant recoveries ($/SF × SF) come from NMRK's underwritten NNN PSF in the DTU, not billed actuals.

redFlags.description: Floor & Decor (51,818 SF, 21% of GLA, $492K base rent) has not opened. Rent commences around Nov-2026, and the Year 1 NOI treats it as in place on the strength of a Seller credit for delivery costs and gap rent. Confirm the lease is executed, the delivery and RCD dates, and that the credit is written into the PSA.

Verizon Wireless (6,420 SF, $303K base) has a lease that expires Jan-2027, but NMRK underwrites a renewal to Jan-2032 based on 'renewal discussions', not a signed amendment. Its $47.21 PSF in-place rent sits above NMRK's own $45 market rent.
Two restaurants roll in Year 1 with no options: Flaming Grill of Tao (10,334 SF, Dec-2027) and Santa Rosa (Nov-2027). Together that is 13,202 SF and about $300K of base rent at renewal risk.
The four Kmart-demise anchors (Lidl, Ollie's, Goodwill, Harbor Freight = 95,727 SF, 40% of GLA) all expire between Mar-2031 and Oct-2031, so their option decisions fall inside a 5–7 year hold.

Year 1 real estate taxes are underwritten at $625,819, up 25% from FY2025 actuals of $500,040. Maryland reassesses on a 3-year cycle and a sale can reset the base, so get an independent tax forecast. The OM itself tells investors to consult a tax consultant.
FY2025 NOI of $3.73M includes $230,740 of 'Other Income' that looks non-recurring. On a like-for-like basis, the step up to $4.20M Year 1 NOI comes mostly from the new Floor & Decor rent.
Atlantic Union Bank pays $72.55 PSF, well above typical inline rent (NMRK market $85). It has no options and expires Apr-2032.

upsideItems.detail: Four owned pads (Atlantic Union Bank, Burger King, Gogi-Go, Aspen Dental/Starbucks) could be sold at accretive cap rates, lowering the basis on the rest of the center.
The seven major tenants (78% of GLA) average $12.85 PSF, a low and replicable basis in a submarket with no competitive box vacancies and none delivered this cycle.
Flaming Grill of Tao and Santa Rosa can re-lease without option constraints. NMRK marks Flaming Grill to $22.51 (+27%).
The last vacancy (1,975 SF) is underwritten at $33.77 PSF from Jan-2028.

deals.notes: Frederick County Square is a 242,282 SF grocery-anchored community center on 21 acres at 1003 W Patrick St on Frederick, Maryland's 'Golden Mile' (Route 40, 47,500 VPD), half a mile west of the U.S. 15 interchange (~102,000 VPD). The center was built in 1973 and repositioned in 2019–2021, when the former Kmart was demised into Lidl (the only Lidl within 20 miles), Ollie's, Goodwill and Harbor Freight. Floor & Decor (51,818 SF, lease through 2036) is backfilling the former JoAnn box with an est. Nov-2026 opening, and Advance Auto expanded in 2025. The property is 99.2% leased (one 1,975 SF vacancy). WALT is 6.3 years, average in-place base rent is $18.13 PSF, and the seven majors average just $12.85 PSF. NMRK underwrites Year 1 NOI of $4,195,339, growing at a 2.8% 10-year CAGR. The trade area is dense and affluent: 92,203 people within 3 miles (projected +9.7% by 2030) with a $118,989 average household income, and $133,714 within 5 miles. Eleven competing centers are 98.4% occupied, with no competitive box vacancy in the submarket. The thesis is a low, replicable anchor rent basis plus pad spin-off optionality (four owned pads). The asset is offered unpriced. The main risks are the Floor & Decor delivery and gap rent (credited by the Seller at closing), an unsigned Verizon renewal, the concentration of Kmart-demise anchor expirations in 2031, and a 25% jump in underwritten taxes over FY2025. Normalized for non-recurring FY2025 other income, the step up from historical NOI ($3.73M FY2025) relies mostly on the new Floor & Decor lease.
